original.target_description: Experiment 1; all 100 Cornell undergraduates; erotic picture-location hit rate versus chance (50%), one-tailed one-sample t test.

n.location: p. 409, Experiment 1, Results and Discussion; Method begins p. 408
n.sample_role: participants, each contributing one session; analytic n supported by t(99)
n.exclusions: No exclusions reported for this test; all 100 sessions included.

p.location: p. 409, Experiment 1, Results and Discussion; footnote 3

replication.target_description: Women-only replication of Experiment 1, erotic-picture accuracy against chance; combined sessions 1 and 2, sixth preregistered Bayesian analysis.

n.location: Supplement p. 2, immediately before six confirmatory analyses
n.quote:
we tested 100 participants who each
contributed two sessions.
n.sample_role: participants (women); two contiguous sessions per participant
n.exclusions: No exclusions documented; supplement confirms 100 participants contributed two sessions.

es.quote: With the default prior, the data are 16.6 times more likely under H0 than under H1
es.test_statistic: BF01 = 16.6; BF02 = 6.2 (Bayes factors, not effect sizes)

p.quote: We decided in advance not to compute p values

reported_success.quote: The evidence (i.e., the logarithm of the Bayes factor) supports H0 (“performance for erotic stimuli does not differ from chance”).

notes: Original values use the same one-sample t test; printed significance levels are one-tailed (footnote 3). Replication reports Bayes factors rather than an effect size or p value; no conversion performed. Supplement acquired and checked: its test 6 heading identifies erotic versus chance, but body and caption repeat neutral-versus-erotic wording from test 5. Main article explicitly defines test 6 as erotic versus chance, combined sessions, and is used for the test identity.
